questions.knowledge_point: Applying the Extreme Value Theorem to Piecewise Functions
questions.problem:
Suppose that $f(x)$ is defined as

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{2}^{-x}, & x\ge 0 \\ -1, & x<0.\end{aligned}
$$

On which of the following intervals can the extreme value theorem be applied to the function?

I. $[-1,1]$

II. $[\frac{1}{2},1]$

III. $[-1,0)$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the extreme value theorem is only applicable to closed intervals on which the function is continuous.

So, let's check whether the function is continuous on each of the intervals.

- First, consider $[-1,1].$ In this case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 0}({2}^{-x})={2}^{0}=1, \\ {lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(-1)=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the limits from the left and from the right of $x=0$ are not the same. Hence, $f(x)$ has a discontinuity at $x=0.$ Therefore, $f(x)$ is not continuous on the interval $[-1,1],$ and the extreme value theorem is not applicable on this interval.

- Now, consider the interval $[\frac{1}{2},1].$ In this interval, $f(x)={2}^{-x}$ and so $f(x)$ is continuous on $[\frac{1}{2},1].$  Therefore, the extreme value theorem is applicable on this interval.

- Finally, the interval $[-1,0)$, is not closed, so the extreme value theorem is not applicable in this case.

In conclusion, the correct answer is "II only".

evidence.solution_quote: In conclusion, the correct answer is "II only".

questions.problem:
Suppose that $f(x)$ is defined as

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2, & x<0 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

On which of the following intervals can the extreme value theorem be applied to the function?

I. $[-\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}]$

II. $[\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{\pi }{3}]$

III. $[\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{2\pi }{3}]$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the extreme value theorem is only applicable to closed intervals on which the function is continuous.

So, let's check whether the function is continuous on each of the intervals.

- Consider $[-\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}].$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 0}2=2, \\ {lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\operatorname{tan}⁡x=0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the limits from the left and from the right of $x=0$ are not the same. Hence, $f(x)$ has a discontinuity at $x=0.$ Therefore, $f(x)$ is not continuous on the interval $[-\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}],$ and the extreme value theorem is not applicable on this interval.

- Consider $[\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{\pi }{3}].$ In this interval, $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡x,$ so the function $f(x)$ is continuous on the interval $[\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{\pi }{3}],$ and the extreme value theorem is applicable on this interval.

- Consider $[\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{2\pi }{3}].$ In this interval, $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡x,$ so the function is not defined at $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Therefore, $f(x)$ is not continuous on the interval $[\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{2\pi }{3}],$ and the extreme value theorem is not applicable on this interval.

In conclusion, the correct answer is "II only".
